influence.definition: To have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
influence.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition! Do NOT use 'on' after the verb 'influence'. However, the noun 'influence' DOES take 'on'.
influence.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'It influences me' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'It has an influence ON me' (uses ON)
examples: Weather can strongly influence people's mood.
His speeches influenced millions of voters.
influence.common_mistake: ❌ It influences on my decision. ➔ ✅ It influences my decision. (OR: It has an influence on my decision.)

affect.definition: To produce a change or influence in someone or something.
affect.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'on'. (Note: The noun 'effect' takes 'on').
affect.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Climate change affects wildlife' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'It has an effect ON wildlife' (uses ON)
examples: The new tax laws will affect small business owners.
Lack of sleep negatively affects your health.
affect.common_mistake: ❌ Smoking affects on health. ➔ ✅ Smoking affects health. (OR: Smoking has an effect on health.)

impact.definition: To have a strong effect or influence on someone or something.
impact.grammar_rule: As a verb, 'impact' can take a direct object or 'on'. As a noun, it always takes 'on'.
impact.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'This policy impacts local business' ➔ Noun: 'This policy has an impact ON local business'
examples: The decision will impact on future generations.
Technology heavily impacts our daily routines.
impact.common_mistake: ❌ A negative impact for society. ➔ ✅ A negative impact on society.

answer.definition: To say, write, or do something as a reaction to a question, call, or letter.
answer.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' when answering a question/person. However, the noun 'answer' takes 'to'.
answer.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'I answered her question' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'Here is the answer TO her question' (uses TO)
examples: Please answer the phone.
He answered all my questions patiently.
answer.common_mistake: ❌ She answered to my email. ➔ ✅ She answered my email. (OR: She sent an answer to my email.)

contact.definition: To communicate or get in touch with someone by phone, email, or letter.
contact.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition. However, the phrase 'be in contact' takes 'with'.
contact.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Contact me tomorrow' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'Keep in contact WITH me' (uses WITH)
examples: Please contact customer support for assistance.
I will contact you as soon as I arrive.
contact.common_mistake: ❌ Contact with me later. ➔ ✅ Contact me later.

visit.definition: To go to see a person or place for pleasure, business, or social reasons.
visit.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT use 'to'. However, the noun 'visit' takes 'to'.
visit.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'We visited Rome last summer' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'We paid a visit TO Rome' (uses TO)
examples: We visited our grandparents last weekend.
Thousands of tourists visit the museum every day.
visit.common_mistake: ❌ I visited to London. ➔ ✅ I visited London. (OR: I went on a visit to London.)

approach.definition: To come near or nearer to someone or something in distance or time.
approach.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to'. However, the noun 'approach' takes 'to'.
approach.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'The train approached the station' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'Our approach TO the problem' (uses TO)
examples: As winter approaches, temperatures drop.
A stranger approached me on the street.
approach.common_mistake: ❌ He approached to the manager. ➔ ✅ He approached the manager.

lack.definition: To not have or not have enough of something.
lack.grammar_rule: As a verb, 'lack' takes a direct object (no preposition). As a noun, 'lack' takes 'of'.
lack.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He lacks confidence' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'A lack OF confidence' (uses OF)
examples: The applicant lacks relevant work experience.
She never lacks creative ideas.
lack.common_mistake: ❌ He lacks of experience. ➔ ✅ He lacks experience. (OR: He suffers from a lack of experience.)

demand.definition: To ask for something authoritatively or forcefully.
demand.grammar_rule: Verb takes a direct object without preposition. Noun 'demand' takes 'for'.
demand.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'They demand higher wages' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'There is a high demand FOR workers' (uses FOR)
examples: Workers demand fair compensation.
The customer demanded an immediate refund.
demand.common_mistake: ❌ They demanded for an answer. ➔ ✅ They demanded an answer.

request.definition: To ask for something politely or formally.
request.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition. Noun 'request' takes 'for'.
request.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She requested assistance' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'A request FOR assistance' (uses FOR)
examples: Passengers are requested to remain seated.
I requested a copy of the official transcript.
request.common_mistake: ❌ I requested for a room upgrade. ➔ ✅ I requested a room upgrade.

arrive.pattern: arrive at [building / station] OR arrive in [city / country]
arrive.grammar_rule: Use 'arrive AT' for buildings, stations, airports, events. Use 'arrive IN' for cities, countries, towns. NEVER use 'to'!
examples: We arrived at the airport two hours early.
They arrived in Tokyo yesterday evening.
arrive.common_mistake: ❌ We arrived to London. ➔ ✅ We arrived in London.

agree.pattern: agree with [person] / agree on [topic] / agree to [proposal]
agree.definition: To share the same opinion or accept a proposal.
agree.grammar_rule: Use 'with' for people, 'on/about' for topics/terms, and 'to' for plans/terms/requests.
examples: I completely agree with you.
They agreed on the price.
She agreed to our terms.
agree.common_mistake: ❌ I am agree with you. ➔ ✅ I agree with you.

ask.definition: To inquire about something or request an item/favor.
ask.grammar_rule: 'Ask someone' (direct object for question/person); 'ask FOR something' when requesting an item or help.
examples: If you need help, don't hesitate to ask for it.
Can I ask you a question?
She asked about your health.
ask.common_mistake: ❌ Ask to the teacher a question. ➔ ✅ Ask the teacher a question.

pay.definition: To give money for goods, services, or debts.
pay.grammar_rule: Direct object for the bill/money ('pay the bill'); use 'FOR' when specifying the item bought ('pay for the coffee').
examples: How much did you pay for that jacket?
I will pay the bill.
Pay attention to the details!
pay.common_mistake: ❌ Pay the coffee. ➔ ✅ Pay for the coffee.

believe.pattern: believe [someone / statement] (VT) / believe in [god / concept / oneself] (VI)
believe.definition: To accept something as true, or have faith/trust in something.
believe.grammar_rule: Transitive direct 'believe someone' = trust their words. Intransitive 'believe IN someone' = trust their character/existence.
examples: Do you believe in magic?
I believe every word she said.
Always believe in yourself.
believe.common_mistake: ❌ I believe in what you said. ➔ ✅ I believe what you said.

worry.definition: To feel anxious or uneasy about actual or potential problems.
worry.grammar_rule: Intransitive uses 'about'. Passive / state form: 'be worried ABOUT'.
examples: Don't worry about the future.
Parents always worry about their children.
worry.common_mistake: ❌ Don't worry for this. ➔ ✅ Don't worry about this.

laugh.definition: To make sounds and facial movements expressing amusement or ridicule.
laugh.grammar_rule: Requires 'at' when directed at a person, joke, or situation.
examples: Everyone laughed at his hilarious joke.
Don't laugh at other people's mistakes.
laugh.common_mistake: ❌ Don't laugh on him. ➔ ✅ Don't laugh at him.

look at.definition: To direct your eyes toward someone or something to see them.
look at.grammar_rule: Requires 'at' when specifying the target of sight.
examples: Look at that beautiful painting on the wall!
She looked at me and smiled.
look at.common_mistake: ❌ Look to the board! ➔ ✅ Look at the board!

look for.definition: To attempt to find someone or something that is lost or needed.
examples: I am looking for my car keys.
Are you looking for a new job?
look for.common_mistake: ❌ I am looking my keys. ➔ ✅ I am looking for my keys.

look after.definition: To take care of or be responsible for someone or something.
look after.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb. Equivalent to 'take care of'.
examples: Could you look after my cat while I am away?
Nurses look after hospital patients around the clock.
look after.common_mistake: ❌ Look after of the baby. ➔ ✅ Look after the baby.

take care of.definition: To protect, mind, or handle responsibility for someone or something.
examples: She takes care of her elderly parents.
Don't worry about the bill; I will take care of it.
take care of.common_mistake: ❌ Take care for him. ➔ ✅ Take care of him.

think of.definition: To produce an idea or hold an opinion about something.
think of.grammar_rule: 'Think OF' is used for opinions ('What do you think of X?') or spontaneous ideas ('I thought of a plan').
examples: What do you think of his new proposal?
I can't think of her name right now.
think of.common_mistake: ❌ What do you think about the movie? (when asking overall impression) ➔ ✅ What do you think of the movie?

think about.definition: To consider or reflect deeply on something over a period of time.
think about.grammar_rule: 'Think ABOUT' implies active mental consideration or deliberation.
examples: I need some time to think about your offer.
What are you thinking about so intently?
think about.common_mistake: ❌ I am thinking to buy a house. ➔ ✅ I am thinking about buying a house.

depend.definition: To be controlled, decided, or influenced by someone or something else.
depend.grammar_rule: Always requires the preposition 'on' (or formal 'upon') before a noun or gerund object.
examples: Our weekend plans depend on the weather.
Children depend on their parents for love and security.
depend.common_mistake: ❌ It depends of the situation. ➔ ✅ It depends on the situation.

apologize.definition: To express regret or say sorry for doing something wrong.
apologize.grammar_rule: Use 'to' before the person receiving the apology, and 'for' before the reason or gerund (-ing).
examples: He apologized to his colleagues for being late.
You should apologize for making that remark.
apologize.common_mistake: ❌ He apologized me. ➔ ✅ He apologized to me.

discuss.definition: To talk about something in detail with someone.
discuss.grammar_rule: Strictly transitive direct verb! Do NOT add 'about' after 'discuss'.
examples: We need to discuss the new budget in tomorrow's meeting.
They discussed the problem openly.
discuss.common_mistake: ❌ We discussed about the project. ➔ ✅ We discussed the project.

look forward to.definition: To feel excited or pleased about something that is going to happen.
look forward to.grammar_rule: Inseparable 3-part phrasal verb. 'To' is a preposition; always follow with a noun or gerund (-ing).
examples: I look forward to meeting you next week.
She is looking forward to her summer vacation.
look forward to.common_mistake: ❌ I look forward to meet you. ➔ ✅ I look forward to meeting you.

listen.definition: To pay attention to sound or give attention to someone speaking.
listen.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' when followed by an object. Without an object, 'listen' stands alone.
examples: I love listening to jazz music in the evening.
Please listen to the teacher carefully.

turn down.pattern: turn down [something] OR turn [something / pronoun] down
turn down.definition: To reject an offer or invitation, or to reduce the volume/heat.
turn down.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb! Noun objects can go before or after 'down', but pronoun objects MUST go in between (e.g. 'turn IT down').
examples: She turned down the job offer in Paris.
Please turn the music down before midnight.
They offered him a promotion, but he turned it down.
turn down.common_mistake: ❌ He turned down it. ➔ ✅ He turned it down.

give up.pattern: give up [habit/item] / give [it] up / give up (intransitive)
give up.definition: To stop doing or having something, or to stop trying.
give up.grammar_rule: Transitive direct when stopping a habit (separable: 'give it up'). Intransitive when quitting effort ('Never give up!').
examples: He gave up smoking after ten years.
Don't give up! You are so close to solving the puzzle.
It was hard, but she finally gave it up.
give up.common_mistake: ❌ He gave up it last year. ➔ ✅ He gave it up last year.

carry on.definition: To continue doing something without stopping.
carry on.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb. Followed by gerund (-ing) or 'with' + noun.
examples: Please carry on with your work while I am out.
Despite the rain, they carried on playing football.
carry on.common_mistake: ❌ Carry on to read the book. ➔ ✅ Carry on reading the book.

look up to.definition: To admire and respect someone as a role model.
look up to.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb. Always follow with 'to' + person.
examples: Young athletes look up to professional players for inspiration.
She has always looked up to her older sister.
look up to.common_mistake: ❌ He looks up at his teacher for guidance. ➔ ✅ He looks up to his teacher for guidance.

break down.definition: To stop functioning (machinery/vehicle) or lose emotional control.
break down.grammar_rule: Purely intransitive phrasal verb when referring to mechanical failure or emotional tears.
examples: Our car broke down on the motorway.
She broke down in tears when she heard the touching news.
break down.common_mistake: ❌ The engine broke down us. ➔ ✅ The engine broke down.

run out of.definition: To use up all of something so that none is left.
run out of.grammar_rule: Inseparable 2-particle phrasal verb requiring 'of' before the exhausted supply.
examples: We ran out of milk this morning during breakfast.
Hurry up! We are running out of time.
run out of.common_mistake: ❌ We ran out from gas. ➔ ✅ We ran out of gas.

take off.pattern: take off (plane/success - VI) / take off [clothing] (VT separable)
take off.definition: To leave the ground (aircraft), become successful, or remove clothing.
take off.grammar_rule: Intransitive for planes/success ('The plane took off'). Separable transitive for clothing ('take off your coat' / 'take it off').
examples: The flight took off on schedule.
Please take off your shoes before entering.
It was hot, so he took it off.
take off.common_mistake: ❌ Take off it. ➔ ✅ Take it off.

put off.definition: To delay or postpone an event, or discourage someone.
put off.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Nouns can go after or middle; pronouns MUST go in middle ('put it off').
examples: Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
They put off the meeting until next Monday.
Don't let one bad experience put you off.
put off.common_mistake: ❌ Don't put off it. ➔ ✅ Don't put it off.

bring up.definition: To raise a child or to introduce a topic into conversation.
bring up.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Pronoun object MUST split verb and particle ('bring it up').
examples: She was brought up by her grandparents in Scotland.
Why did you bring up that uncomfortable subject at dinner?
It's a delicate topic, so don't bring it up.
bring up.common_mistake: ❌ Don't bring up it now. ➔ ✅ Don't bring it up now.

get along with.definition: To have a harmonious, friendly relationship with someone.
get along with.grammar_rule: Three-part inseparable phrasal verb. Cannot split 'along with'.
examples: Do you get along with your new room-mate?
He gets along well with all his colleagues.
get along with.common_mistake: ❌ I get along my boss. ➔ ✅ I get along with my boss.

call off.definition: To cancel an event, match, or planned agreement.
call off.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Pronoun object must go in middle ('call it off').
examples: They had to call off the football match due to heavy fog.
The strike was called off after negotiations succeeded.
They couldn't agree, so they called it off.
call off.common_mistake: ❌ They called off it. ➔ ✅ They called it off.

come across.definition: To find or meet someone or something by chance.
come across.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb! Do not place the object between 'come' and 'across'.
examples: While cleaning the attic, I came across an old family album.
She came across an interesting article in the magazine.
come across.common_mistake: ❌ I came an old photo across. ➔ ✅ I came across an old photo.

figure out.definition: To understand or solve something after thinking about it.
figure out.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb! 'Figure it out' is the mandatory pronoun placement.
examples: It took me an hour to figure out how to assemble the desk.
Don't worry, we will figure it out together.
figure out.common_mistake: ❌ We must figure out it. ➔ ✅ We must figure it out.

fall out with.definition: To argue with someone and stop being friendly with them.
examples: He fell out with his best friend over a silly argument.
They haven't spoken since they fell out last year.
fall out with.common_mistake: ❌ She fell out her colleague. ➔ ✅ She fell out with her colleague.

set up.definition: To establish a business, organization, system, or equipment.
set up.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. 'Set it up' requires pronoun in the middle.
examples: She set up her own graphic design agency in 2020.
The IT team will set up your laptop this afternoon.
Here is your new router; let's set it up.
set up.common_mistake: ❌ Set up it now. ➔ ✅ Set it up now.

work out.pattern: work out (exercise - VI) / work out [a plan] (VT separable)
work out.definition: To exercise physically (VI), or calculate/solve a problem (VT separable).
work out.grammar_rule: Intransitive for physical fitness. Separable transitive when solving/calculating ('work it out').
examples: I work out at the gym three times a week.
We need to work out a strategy before launching.
The math problem was tough, but he worked it out.
work out.common_mistake: ❌ Work out it carefully. ➔ ✅ Work it out carefully.

catch up with.definition: To reach the same level/position as someone, or meet up to share news.
examples: She ran fast to catch up with the lead runner.
Let's grab coffee this weekend to catch up with each other.
catch up with.common_mistake: ❌ Catch up my friends. ➔ ✅ Catch up with my friends.

keep up with.definition: To move at the same speed as someone, or stay informed about current events.
examples: Slow down! I can't keep up with you.
It is difficult to keep up with rapid technological changes.
keep up with.common_mistake: ❌ Keep up the technology trends. ➔ ✅ Keep up with technological trends.

examples: The room was so hot that two attendees passed out.
He nearly passed out from exhaustion.
pass out.common_mistake: ❌ He passed out the exam. ➔ ✅ He passed out (fainted).

look into.definition: To investigate, research, or examine a problem or situation.
look into.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb! Always put object after 'into'.
examples: The police are looking into the cause of the fire.
Our support team will look into your complaint immediately.
look into.common_mistake: ❌ I will look the complaint into. ➔ ✅ I will look into the complaint.

put up with.definition: To tolerate or endure an unpleasant person or situation without complaining.
examples: I don't know how she puts up with all that noise.
We shouldn't have to put up with rude behavior.
put up with.common_mistake: ❌ Put up the noise. ➔ ✅ Put up with the noise.

go through.definition: To experience a difficult situation, or examine details in documents.
examples: She has gone through a tough time recently.
Let's go through the contract step by step.
go through.common_mistake: ❌ Go the document through. ➔ ✅ Go through the document.

bring about.definition: To cause something to happen or exist.
bring about.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. 'Bring it about' requires pronoun in middle.
examples: New policy changes brought about significant improvement.
What brought about this sudden decision?
bring about.common_mistake: ❌ Bring about it. ➔ ✅ Bring it about.

cut down on.definition: To reduce the amount or quantity of something consumed.
examples: The doctor advised him to cut down on sugar.
We need to cut down on monthly household expenses.
cut down on.common_mistake: ❌ Cut down sugar. ➔ ✅ Cut down on sugar.

get over.definition: To recover from an illness, shock, or emotional difficulty.
get over.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb! Object always follows 'over'.
examples: It took him weeks to get over the flu.
She finally got over her breakup.
get over.common_mistake: ❌ I got the cold over. ➔ ✅ I got over the cold.

grow up.pattern: grow up (in a place / as a child)
grow up.definition: To gradually advance from childhood to adulthood.
grow up.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. (Compare with transitive 'bring up' = raise a child).
examples: He grew up in a small coastal town.
What do you want to be when you grow up?
grow up.common_mistake: ❌ She grew up her child. ➔ ✅ She raised / brought up her child.

show off.pattern: show off (boast - VI) / show off [skills] (VT separable)
show off.definition: To boast or display abilities/possessions proudly to impress others.
show off.grammar_rule: Intransitive when boasting ('Stop showing off!'). Separable transitive ('show off your trophy' / 'show it off').
examples: He loves showing off his sports car.
She bought a new jacket and couldn't wait to show it off.
show off.common_mistake: ❌ Show off it. ➔ ✅ Show it off.

pick up.definition: To lift something, collect a person/item, or learn a skill casually.
pick up.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. 'Pick it up' requires pronoun in middle.
examples: He picked up the heavy box from the floor.
I will pick you up at the station at six.
She picked up conversational Italian while living in Rome.
pick up.common_mistake: ❌ Pick up it. ➔ ✅ Pick it up.

hold on.definition: To wait for a short time, or keep a tight grip on something.
examples: Hold on a minute, I need to tie my shoelace.
Hold on tight to the railing!
hold on.common_mistake: ❌ Hold on the phone me. ➔ ✅ Hold on a second.

back up.definition: To make a copy of computer files, or support a person/claim.
back up.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. 'Back it up' requires pronoun in middle.
examples: Always back up your important documents to the cloud.
My colleagues backed me up during the board meeting.
back up.common_mistake: ❌ Back up it. ➔ ✅ Back it up.

drop out of.definition: To quit a course, school, or competition before completion.
examples: He dropped out of university to start his own software company.
Injuries forced two runners to drop out of the marathon.
drop out of.common_mistake: ❌ Dropped out the school. ➔ ✅ Dropped out of school.

turn up.pattern: turn up (arrive - VI) / turn up [volume/heat] (VT separable)
turn up.definition: To arrive or appear unexpectedly (VI), or increase volume/sound (VT separable).
turn up.grammar_rule: Intransitive for arrival ('He turned up late'). Separable transitive for volume ('turn it up').
examples: He turned up at the party without an invitation.
Could you turn up the radio? I love this song.
Turn it up!
turn up.common_mistake: ❌ Turn up it. ➔ ✅ Turn it up.

work with.definition: To collaborate or cooperate with a team or client on a specific project or objective.
work with.grammar_rule: Multi-preposition structure: work WITH + person/team/company ON + project/task. Note: FOR + noun/gerund expresses purpose, whereas TO + verb infinitive expresses intention.
work with.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'work with a team on a project' ➔ Noun: 'collaboration WITH someone ON something'
examples: He works closely with his team to execute marketing campaigns.
She works with small businesses on social media strategy.
work with.common_mistake: ❌ Work to a team for a project. ➔ ✅ Work with a team on a project.

report to.definition: To be directly responsible to a supervisor, or to provide an account of progress.
report to.grammar_rule: Report TO + person (line manager/supervisor); report ON + subject/progress.
report to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He reports to the head of marketing' ➔ Noun: 'Direct report TO the director'
examples: He reports to the head of marketing and works closely with his team.
The regional managers report directly to the CEO.
report to.common_mistake: ❌ He reports at the manager. ➔ ✅ He reports to the manager.

coordinate with.definition: To organize activities so that people or teams work together effectively.
coordinate with.grammar_rule: Coordinate WITH + person/department ON + task/schedule. Use FOR + noun/gerund when stating the target reason.
coordinate with.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Coordinate with colleagues' ➔ Noun: 'Coordination WITH the team'
examples: She coordinates with her team to meet sales targets.
We need to coordinate with the logistics department on delivery dates.
coordinate with.common_mistake: ❌ Coordinate to the team. ➔ ✅ Coordinate with the team.

responsible for.definition: Having the duty to take care of someone or something, or being the cause of an outcome.
responsible for.grammar_rule: Adjective phrase requiring FOR + noun or gerund (-ing). Do NOT use TO + verb infinitive directly after 'responsible for'.
responsible for.noun_parallel: ⚡ Adjective: 'responsible FOR overseeing' ➔ Noun: 'take responsibility FOR something'
examples: Sarah is responsible for overseeing the entire organization.
Who is responsible for managing customer feedback?
responsible for.common_mistake: ❌ She is responsible to oversee the team. ➔ ✅ She is responsible for overseeing the team.

in charge of.definition: Having control of or responsibility for a department, team, or task.
in charge of.grammar_rule: Prepositional idiom requiring OF + noun or gerund (-ing). Use FOR when expressing purpose separately.
examples: She's in charge of setting the company's vision and goals.
Who is in charge of handling client contracts?
in charge of.common_mistake: ❌ In charge for setting goals. ➔ ✅ In charge of setting goals.

comply with.definition: To act in accordance with a wish, command, law, or rule.
comply with.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure. Always requires 'with'.
comply with.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'comply with safety regulations' ➔ Noun: 'in compliance WITH standards'
examples: All products must comply with international safety standards.
Failure to comply with the rules may result in penalties.
comply with.common_mistake: ❌ Comply to the regulations. ➔ ✅ Comply with the regulations.

specialize in.definition: To concentrate on and become an expert in a particular subject or skill.
specialize in.grammar_rule: Requires 'in' followed by a noun or gerund (-ing).
specialize in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'specialize in corporate law' ➔ Noun: 'specialization IN marketing'
examples: Our firm specializes in environmental law and sustainability.
She specialized in pediatric medicine during residency.
specialize in.common_mistake: ❌ Specialize on international trade. ➔ ✅ Specialize in international trade.

succeed in.definition: To achieve the desired aim or result in a task or career.
succeed in.grammar_rule: Requires 'in' + gerund (-ing). Do NOT use TO + infinitive after 'succeed' when stating the action achieved.
succeed in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'succeed in passing the exam' ➔ Noun: 'success IN business'
examples: She succeeded in securing funding for the new start-up.
If you work hard, you will succeed in achieving your goals.
succeed in.common_mistake: ❌ He succeeded to pass the test. ➔ ✅ He succeeded in passing the test.

attribute to.definition: To regard something as being caused by someone or something.
attribute to.grammar_rule: Complex structure: attribute SOMETHING (direct object) TO SOMETHING/SOMEONE (cause).
attribute to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'attribute success to hard work' ➔ Noun: 'an attribution TO the author'
examples: The CEO attributed the rise in profits to strong teamwork.
Scientists attribute global warming to greenhouse gas emissions.
attribute to.common_mistake: ❌ He attributed the success for his team. ➔ ✅ He attributed the success to his team.

refrain from.definition: To stop oneself from doing something or hold back voluntarily.
refrain from.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'from' + gerund (-ing).
examples: Please refrain from smoking inside the auditorium.
He refrained from making any further comments.
refrain from.common_mistake: ❌ Please refrain to take photos. ➔ ✅ Please refrain from taking photos.

apply.definition: To make a formal request for a job, position, visa, or program.
apply.grammar_rule: Apply FOR + position/thing requested; apply TO + company/institution/person receiving application.
apply.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'apply for a job to a company' ➔ Noun: 'an application FOR a job TO a company'
examples: She applied for a project manager position at Google.
I am applying to three universities in the UK.
apply.common_mistake: ❌ Apply a job to the company. ➔ ✅ Apply for a job at/to the company.

focus on.definition: To give central attention or effort to a particular topic or task.
focus on.grammar_rule: Always requires 'on' before a noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing). Do NOT use 'in' or 'to'.
focus on.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'focus on key priorities' ➔ Noun: 'maintain focus ON priorities'
examples: Let's focus on solving the primary bottleneck first.
He needs to focus on improving his conversational skills.
focus on.common_mistake: ❌ Focus in the project. ➔ ✅ Focus on the project.

rely on.definition: To depend on or trust someone/something to work or act properly.
rely on.grammar_rule: Requires 'on'. Followed by noun, pronoun, or gerund (-ing).
rely on.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'rely on facts' ➔ Noun: 'place reliance ON data'
examples: You can always rely on her to deliver high-quality work on time.
Modern businesses rely heavily on cloud infrastructure.
rely on.common_mistake: ❌ Rely of public transport. ➔ ✅ Rely on public transport.

belong to.definition: To be owned by someone, or be a member of a group.
belong to.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' before the owner or club/organization.
examples: This laptop belongs to the IT department.
Does this notebook belong to you?
belong to.common_mistake: ❌ It belongs for me. ➔ ✅ It belongs to me.

deal with.definition: To take action to handle, resolve, or cope with a situation or person.
examples: Customer service representatives deal with complaints every day.
How do you deal with stress at work?
deal with.common_mistake: ❌ Deal about the issue. ➔ ✅ Deal with the issue.

suffer from.definition: To experience physical or mental pain, illness, or hardship.
suffer from.grammar_rule: Requires 'from' when specifying the medical condition or hardship.
examples: Many adults suffer from chronic sleep deprivation.
The business suffered from severe cash flow problems.
suffer from.common_mistake: ❌ Suffer of migraines. ➔ ✅ Suffer from migraines.

prevent from.definition: To stop something from happening or stop someone from doing an action.
examples: Bad weather prevented us from leaving the port.
Proper security controls prevent hackers from accessing customer data.
prevent from.common_mistake: ❌ Prevent him to enter the building. ➔ ✅ Prevent him from entering the building.

insist on.definition: To demand something forcefully and refuse to accept any refusal.
insist on.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'insist on paying' ➔ Noun: 'an insistence ON quality'
examples: He insisted on paying for everyone's dinner.
Why do you insist on doing everything by yourself?
insist on.common_mistake: ❌ Insist to pay the bill. ➔ ✅ Insist on paying the bill.

participate in.definition: To take part in an event, activity, or conversation.
participate in.grammar_rule: Requires 'in'. Followed by noun or gerund (-ing).
participate in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'participate in workshops' ➔ Noun: 'participation IN discussions'
examples: All team members are encouraged to participate in weekly discussions.
Over fifty countries participated in the climate summit.
participate in.common_mistake: ❌ Participate at the meeting. ➔ ✅ Participate in the meeting.

benefit from.definition: To receive an advantage, profit, or help from something.
benefit from.grammar_rule: Verb 'benefit FROM' takes 'from'. Note: noun 'benefit OF' takes 'of'.
benefit from.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'benefit from training' ➔ Noun: 'the benefit OF experience'
examples: Students benefit from regular personalized feedback.
The local community will benefit greatly from the new sports center.
benefit from.common_mistake: ❌ Benefit of the new system. (when used as verb) ➔ ✅ Benefit from the new system.

approve of.definition: To think that someone or something is good, right, or acceptable.
approve of.grammar_rule: Intransitive + preposition 'of'. Transitive direct 'approve something' means officially sign/authorize.
approve of.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'approve of your choice' ➔ Noun: 'give approval OF/FOR a plan'
examples: Her parents didn't approve of her decision to leave university.
Do you approve of the new office policies?
approve of.common_mistake: ❌ I approve for your plan. ➔ ✅ I approve of your plan.

object to.definition: To express disagreement with or opposition to something.
object to.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' + noun or gerund (-ing). 'To' is a preposition here, NOT an infinitive marker.
object to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'object to changing terms' ➔ Noun: 'raise an objection TO terms'
examples: Several residents object to building a highway near the school.
No one objected to the proposed timetable.
object to.common_mistake: ❌ I object to change the plan. ➔ ✅ I object to changing the plan.

look down on.definition: To consider someone inferior or unworthy of respect.
look down on.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb. Requires 'on' before the target.
examples: She looks down on people who haven't been to university.
You shouldn't look down on manual laborers.
look down on.common_mistake: ❌ She looks down at poor people. ➔ ✅ She looks down on poor people.

come up with.definition: To produce or suggest an idea, plan, or answer.
come up with.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before the idea/plan.
examples: We need to come up with a better marketing strategy.
She came up with a creative solution to the problem.
come up with.common_mistake: ❌ She came up a new plan. ➔ ✅ She came up with a new plan.

get away with.definition: To escape punishment or negative consequences for an action.
get away with.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before the wrongdoing.
examples: He thought he could get away with cheating on the exam.
You can't get away with missing deadlines forever.
get away with.common_mistake: ❌ He got away from cheating. ➔ ✅ He got away with cheating.

face up to.definition: To accept and deal with a difficult situation or reality.
face up to.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'to' before the reality.
examples: You must face up to the fact that we are losing money.
She finally faced up to her responsibilities.
face up to.common_mistake: ❌ He must face up with the truth. ➔ ✅ He must face up to the truth.

stand up for.definition: To defend or support a person, right, or principle.
stand up for.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'for' before the cause/person.
examples: Always stand up for your rights and principles.
He stood up for his friend when others criticized him.
stand up for.common_mistake: ❌ Stand up to your rights! ➔ ✅ Stand up for your rights!

go along with.definition: To agree to or consent to a decision or plan.
go along with.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before the proposal.
examples: I decided to go along with the team's proposal.
She rarely goes along with majority opinions without question.
go along with.common_mistake: ❌ I go along to your plan. ➔ ✅ I go along with your plan.

come down with.definition: To catch or become sick with a minor illness.
come down with.grammar_rule: Inseparable 2-particle phrasal verb + dependent preposition 'with' before the illness.
examples: I think I am coming down with a bad cold.
Half the team came down with flu this week.
come down with.common_mistake: ❌ She came down from a fever. ➔ ✅ She came down with a fever.

get out of.pattern: get out of doing [duty / chore / event]
get out of.definition: To avoid doing a responsibility or duty.
get out of.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb requiring 'of' + gerund (-ing) before the avoided activity.
examples: He tried to get out of doing his household chores.
You cannot get out of attending the mandatory meeting.
get out of.common_mistake: ❌ He got out of to do the work. ➔ ✅ He got out of doing the work.

compete.definition: To strive to gain or win something by defeating others.
compete.grammar_rule: Use 'with' or 'against' before the opponent, and 'for' before the reward/title.
compete.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Compete with rivals' ➔ Noun: 'In competition WITH rivals'
examples: Ten teams will compete against each other for the championship.
Small firms struggle to compete with global tech giants.
compete.common_mistake: ❌ They compete to each other. ➔ ✅ They compete with/against each other.

differ.definition: To be unlike or distinct in nature or quality.
differ.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb requiring 'from' when comparing differences between entities.
differ.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'It differs from that' ➔ Noun: 'There is a difference FROM that'
examples: British English differs from American English in vocabulary.
His second novel differs significantly from his first.
differ.common_mistake: ❌ This model differs to the old one. ➔ ✅ This model differs from the old one.

invest.definition: To put money, time, or energy into something for future benefit.
invest.grammar_rule: Intransitive investment verb requiring 'in' before the asset or venture.
invest.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Invest in stocks' ➔ Noun: 'Make an investment IN stocks'
examples: The company is investing in renewable energy technology.
It is wise to invest in employee training.
invest.common_mistake: ❌ They invested on real estate. ➔ ✅ They invested in real estate.

consist of.definition: To be composed or made up of specified elements.
consist of.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb requiring 'of' (do not confuse with 'comprise' which takes no prep).
examples: The committee consists of ten elected representatives.
A healthy breakfast should consist of protein and fiber.
consist of.common_mistake: ❌ The team consists from six members. ➔ ✅ The team consists of six members.

congratulate.definition: To express praise or good wishes to someone for an achievement.
congratulate.grammar_rule: Direct object person first, followed strictly by 'on' + achievement (NEVER 'for'!).
congratulate.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Congratulate him on passing' ➔ Noun: 'Congratulations ON passing'
examples: I congratulated her on winning the prestigious award.
They congratulated the team on their promotion.
congratulate.common_mistake: ❌ I congratulated him for his wedding. ➔ ✅ I congratulated him on his wedding.

warn.definition: To inform someone in advance of impending danger or trouble.
warn.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb taking 'about' or 'of' before the hazard, or 'against' before an action.
warn.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Warn them about storm' ➔ Noun: 'Issue a warning ABOUT storm'
examples: Scientists warned the public about the approaching storm.
She warned me against investing without research.
warn.common_mistake: ❌ They warned to us about the risk. ➔ ✅ They warned us about the risk.

protect.definition: To keep someone or something safe from harm or damage.
protect.grammar_rule: Direct object first, followed by 'from' or 'against' before the danger source.
protect.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Protect skin from sun' ➔ Noun: 'Protection FROM sun'
examples: Sunscreen helps protect your skin from harmful UV rays.
The new law aims to protect consumers against fraud.
protect.common_mistake: ❌ Protect kids to danger. ➔ ✅ Protect kids from danger.

embark on.definition: To start or initiate a new project, journey, or enterprise.
embark on.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'on' or 'upon'.
examples: She is about to embark on a new career in journalism.
The country embarked on a series of economic reforms.
embark on.common_mistake: ❌ They embarked in a new adventure. ➔ ✅ They embarked on a new adventure.

capitalize on.definition: To take advantage of an opportunity or situation for profit or success.
capitalize on.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition requiring 'on' before the opportunity.
examples: The tech company capitalized on the surging demand for AI software.
He capitalized on his opponent's mistake to win the match.
capitalize on.common_mistake: ❌ Capitalize from the opportunity. ➔ ✅ Capitalize on the opportunity.

dispose of.definition: To get rid of, throw away, or sell something.
dispose of.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Dispose of waste safely' ➔ Noun: 'Waste disposal (no prep)'
examples: Hazardous chemicals must be disposed of carefully.
The business disposed of its non-core assets.
dispose of.common_mistake: ❌ Dispose off toxic waste. ➔ ✅ Dispose of toxic waste.

resort to.definition: To turn to a extreme or unpleasant strategy because no other options remain.
resort to.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure. 'To' is a preposition, followed by noun or gerund.
examples: They had to resort to legal action to recover the money.
Never resort to violence to solve personal conflicts.
resort to.common_mistake: ❌ Resort into extreme measures. ➔ ✅ Resort to extreme measures.

contribute to.definition: To help bring about a result or donate toward a common purpose.
contribute to.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' before the recipient, outcome, or cause.
contribute to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Contribute to research' ➔ Noun: 'Make a contribution TO research'
examples: Pollution contributes significantly to climate change.
Many volunteers contributed to the success of the event.
contribute to.common_mistake: ❌ Smoking contributes for lung disease. ➔ ✅ Smoking contributes to lung disease.

adhere to.definition: To stick firmly to a rule, agreement, or belief.
adhere to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Adhere to guidelines' ➔ Noun: 'Strict adherence TO guidelines'
examples: All members must strictly adhere to the company code of conduct.
She adhered to her diet despite temptations.
adhere to.common_mistake: ❌ Adhere with the safety rules. ➔ ✅ Adhere to the safety rules.

conform to.definition: To comply with rules, standards, or social expectations.
conform to.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'to' (or 'with') before the standard being met.
conform to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Conform to standards' ➔ Noun: 'In conformity WITH standards'
examples: The new building design conforms to all fire safety regulations.
Pressure to conform to social norms can be strong.
conform to.common_mistake: ❌ Conform by the regulations. ➔ ✅ Conform to the regulations.

cope with.definition: To deal effectively with something difficult or challenging.
cope with.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition requiring 'with'. NEVER say 'cope up with'!
examples: How do you cope with high levels of work stress?
She coped remarkably well with the sudden loss.
cope with.common_mistake: ❌ I cannot cope up with this pressure. ➔ ✅ I cannot cope with this pressure.

deviate from.definition: To depart from an established course, standard, or topic.
deviate from.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Deviate from protocol' ➔ Noun: 'A deviation FROM protocol'
examples: The pilot had to deviate from the planned flight path due to weather.
We must not deviate from our original budget.
deviate from.common_mistake: ❌ Do not deviate to the protocol. ➔ ✅ Do not deviate from the protocol.

indulge in.definition: To allow oneself to enjoy the pleasure of something, often excessively.
indulge in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Indulge in sweets' ➔ Noun: 'Self-indulgence IN sweets'
examples: On weekends she likes to indulge in a long spa day.
They indulged in luxury shopping during their vacation.
indulge in.common_mistake: ❌ Indulge with fine dining. ➔ ✅ Indulge in fine dining.

prevail over.definition: To prove superior in power or influence and triumph over an opponent.
prevail over.grammar_rule: Intransitive formal verb requiring 'over' or 'against' before the defeated entity.
examples: Truth and justice will eventually prevail over corruption.
Our team prevailed over strong competitors in the final.
prevail over.common_mistake: ❌ Justice prevailed against of tyranny. ➔ ✅ Justice prevailed over tyranny.

dwell on.definition: To think or speak about a painful subject at length.
dwell on.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition structure requiring 'on' or 'upon'.
examples: There is no point in dwelling on past mistakes.
Try not to dwell on negative thoughts.
dwell on.common_mistake: ❌ Don't dwell in your failures. ➔ ✅ Don't dwell on your failures.

hinge on.definition: To depend entirely on a crucial factor or decision.
examples: The success of the deal hinges on tomorrow's vote.
Everything hinges on securing adequate funding.
hinge on.common_mistake: ❌ The plan hinges from approval. ➔ ✅ The plan hinges on approval.

culminate in.definition: To reach a climax or highest point of development in a specified result.
culminate in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Culminate in success' ➔ Noun: 'Reach its culmination IN success'
examples: Years of research culminated in a major medical breakthrough.
The festival culminated in a spectacular fireworks show.
culminate in.common_mistake: ❌ Culminate into a climax. ➔ ✅ Culminate in a climax.

account for.definition: To explain the cause of something or constitute a portion of a total.
examples: Housing costs account for 40% of her monthly budget.
How do you account for this unexpected loss?
account for.common_mistake: ❌ Account about the discrepancy. ➔ ✅ Account for the discrepancy.

strive for.definition: To make great efforts to achieve or obtain something.
strive for.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'for' before the desired target or excellence.
examples: Our company strives for excellence in customer service.
Athletes constantly strive for peak physical performance.
strive for.common_mistake: ❌ Strive to excellence. ➔ ✅ Strive for excellence.

stem from.definition: To originate or develop as a result of something.
stem from.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb + preposition requiring 'from' before the root cause.
examples: His anxiety stems from past traumatic experiences.
Many health problems stem from poor dietary habits.
stem from.common_mistake: ❌ The error stems out of ignorance. ➔ ✅ The error stems from ignorance.

subjugate to.definition: To bring under domination or control.
subjugate to.grammar_rule: Direct object first, followed by 'to' before the controlling entity.
examples: The empire subjugated neighboring tribes to its central rule.
Personal desires were subjugated to the common good.
subjugate to.common_mistake: ❌ Subjugate under authority. ➔ ✅ Subjugate to authority.

pertain to.definition: To relate to or have a direct connection with something.
pertain to.grammar_rule: Inseparable formal verb taking 'to' before the related subject.
examples: These documents pertain to the recent merger negotiations.
The regulations pertain to all international flights.
pertain to.common_mistake: ❌ Pertain with the case. ➔ ✅ Pertain to the case.

resign from.definition: To formally give up one's job, office, or position.
resign from.grammar_rule: Intransitive career verb requiring 'from' before the position relinquished.
resign from.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Resign from post' ➔ Noun: 'Hand in resignation FROM post'
examples: The CEO resigned from his post amid public scrutiny.
She decided to resign from the board of directors.
resign from.common_mistake: ❌ He resigned of his job. ➔ ✅ He resigned from his job.

abide by.definition: To accept and comply with a rule, decision, or recommendation.
abide by.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb requiring 'by' (NEVER use 'with' or 'to'!).
examples: Both players agreed to abide by the referee's decision.
Visitors must abide by the park regulations.
abide by.common_mistake: ❌ Abide to the law. ➔ ✅ Abide by the law.

cater to.definition: To provide what is needed or desired by a specific group.
cater to.grammar_rule: Use 'cater to' for preferences or demands, and 'cater for' when providing food/services for events.
examples: The resort caters to luxury travelers seeking privacy.
The cafeteria caters for vegetarians and vegans.
cater to.common_mistake: ❌ The hotel caters with rich tourists. ➔ ✅ The hotel caters to rich tourists.

tamper with.definition: To interfere with something in an unauthorized or harmful way.
examples: Someone tried to tamper with the security lock.
It is a crime to tamper with official evidence.
tamper with.common_mistake: ❌ Tamper on the machinery. ➔ ✅ Tamper with the machinery.

discriminate against.definition: To treat someone unfairly based on category, or distinguish between things.
discriminate against.grammar_rule: Use 'against' for unfair prejudice, and 'between' when making a distinction.
discriminate against.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Discriminate against minority' ➔ Noun: 'Discrimination AGAINST minority'
examples: Laws prohibit employers from discriminating against job applicants.
Can you discriminate between genuine and fake notes?
discriminate against.common_mistake: ❌ Discriminate to elderly workers. ➔ ✅ Discriminate against elderly workers.

substitute for.definition: To use or act in place of another person or thing.
substitute for.grammar_rule: Use 'substitute A for B' (A replaces B). Do not confuse with 'replace B with A'.
substitute for.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Substitute butter for oil' ➔ Noun: 'A substitute FOR oil'
examples: You can substitute honey for sugar in this recipe.
A assistant teacher substituted for the professor today.
substitute for.common_mistake: ❌ Substitute sugar by honey. ➔ ✅ Substitute honey for sugar.

interfere with.definition: To hinder or disrupt a process, or meddle in private affairs.
interfere with.grammar_rule: Use 'interfere with' for disruption of processes, and 'interfere in' for unwanted intrusion into affairs.
interfere with.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Interfere with work' ➔ Noun: 'Interference WITH work'
examples: Loud music can interfere with your concentration.
Stop trying to interfere in my personal life!
interfere with.common_mistake: ❌ Interfere to my business. ➔ ✅ Interfere in my business.

impinge on.definition: To encroach or have an intrusive effect on someone's rights or privacy.
examples: The proposed surveillance law impinges on personal privacy.
New regulations must not impinge upon academic freedom.
impinge on.common_mistake: ❌ Impinge to civil liberties. ➔ ✅ Impinge on civil liberties.

infringe on.definition: To violate or trespass upon a law, right, or agreement.
infringe on.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Infringe on copyright' ➔ Noun: 'An infringement ON copyright'
examples: Copying this software infringes on patent rights.
Do not infringe upon the freedom of speech.
infringe on.common_mistake: ❌ Infringe against my copyright. ➔ ✅ Infringe on my copyright.

deliberate on.definition: To carefully discuss or consider a issue or decision.
deliberate on.grammar_rule: Can take a direct object or 'on'/'over' before the subject of deliberation.
examples: The jury deliberated on the verdict for three days.
The committee is deliberating over the proposed policy.
deliberate on.common_mistake: ❌ Deliberate about the verdict for days. ➔ ✅ Deliberate on the verdict.

prevail upon.definition: To persuade or convince someone to do something.
prevail upon.grammar_rule: Transitive formal verb requiring 'upon' or 'on' + person + infinitive.
examples: We managed to prevail upon him to stay for dinner.
She prevailed upon her colleagues to support the motion.
prevail upon.common_mistake: ❌ Prevail to him to join us. ➔ ✅ Prevail upon him to join us.

yield to.definition: To give way to pressure, force, or superior authority.
yield to.grammar_rule: Inseparable verb requiring 'to' before the force surrendered to.
examples: The government refused to yield to terrorist demands.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic at the roundabout.
yield to.common_mistake: ❌ Yield for traffic on the left. ➔ ✅ Yield to traffic on the left.

succumb to.definition: To fail to resist pressure, temptation, or illness.
examples: He succumbed to his injuries two days after the accident.
Do not succumb to temptation when dieting.
succumb to.common_mistake: ❌ Succumb from illness. ➔ ✅ Succumb to illness.

ascribe to.definition: To attribute a cause, quality, or motive to someone or something.
ascribe to.grammar_rule: Transitive formal verb requiring 'to' before the attributed cause or person.
examples: They ascribe the artwork's value to its rarity.
Scholars ascribe this poem to Shakespeare.
ascribe to.common_mistake: ❌ Ascribe motive for his actions. ➔ ✅ Ascribe motive to his actions.

conduce to.definition: To help bring about or contribute to a desirable outcome.
conduce to.grammar_rule: Inseparable formal verb taking 'to' before the resulting state.
examples: Good health habits conduce to long life and happiness.
A quiet environment conduces to productive study.
conduce to.common_mistake: ❌ Conduce for well-being. ➔ ✅ Conduce to well-being.

coincide with.definition: To happen at the same time or correspond in nature.
coincide with.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Coincide with holiday' ➔ Noun: 'A coincidence WITH holiday'
examples: Our trip was planned to coincide with the summer festival.
His views on politics coincide with mine.
coincide with.common_mistake: ❌ Coincide to the meeting time. ➔ ✅ Coincide with the meeting time.

go.definition: To move or travel from one place to another.
go.grammar_rule: Intransitive motion verb requiring 'to' before a destination (except 'home' or 'there').
examples: I go to school by bus every morning.
We are going to Paris next weekend.
go.common_mistake: ❌ I go at school every day. ➔ ✅ I go to school every day.

come.definition: To move toward a place or originate from a place.
come.grammar_rule: Intransitive motion verb taking 'to' for destination and 'from' for origin.
examples: She comes to work at eight o'clock.
They come from a small town in Spain.
come.common_mistake: ❌ She comes in my house. ➔ ✅ She comes to my house.

get.definition: To arrive at or reach a location.
get.grammar_rule: Intransitive when meaning 'arrive'. Use 'to' before a location (except 'home' or 'there').
examples: How do you get to the train station?
I usually get to the office around nine.
get.common_mistake: ❌ How do I get in the office? ➔ ✅ How do I get to the office?

look.definition: To direct eyes toward a specific person or object.
look.grammar_rule: Intransitive visual verb requiring 'at' when specifying the target of sight.
look.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Look at the board' ➔ Noun: 'Take a look AT the board'
examples: Look at that big dog over there!
Please look at page ten in your book.
look.common_mistake: ❌ Look to the board! ➔ ✅ Look at the board!

wait for.definition: To stay in a place until an expected person or event arrives.
wait for.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb requiring 'for' when specifying the expected person or event.
examples: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.
She waited for her friend for thirty minutes.
wait for.common_mistake: ❌ I am waiting my friend. ➔ ✅ I am waiting for my friend.

talk.definition: To speak to someone or converse about a subject.
talk.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'to' or 'with' for the listener and 'about' for the topic.
examples: I need to talk to my manager about my schedule.
They talked about their favorite movies for hours.
talk.common_mistake: ❌ We talked the problem. ➔ ✅ We talked about the problem.

speak.definition: To communicate orally with someone or address a topic.
speak.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'to' or 'with' for the listener and 'about' for the topic.
examples: May I speak to the manager, please?
The professor spoke about history in class.
speak.common_mistake: ❌ Can I speak with you about? ➔ ✅ Can I speak with you about this issue?

thank.definition: To express gratitude to someone for a helpful action or gift.
thank.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Place the person immediately after 'thank', then use 'for' before the reason.
thank.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'I thanked him for his help' ➔ Noun: 'My thanks FOR his help'
examples: We thanked our host for the wonderful dinner.
She thanked me for helping her move.
thank.common_mistake: ❌ Thank to you for coming. ➔ ✅ Thank you for coming.

hope.definition: To want something to happen or be true.
hope.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'for' before a desired outcome or noun.
examples: We are hoping for sunny weather tomorrow.
They hoped for good news from the doctor.
hope.common_mistake: ❌ We hope of good weather. ➔ ✅ We hope for good weather.

smile.definition: To form a pleased facial expression directed toward someone.
smile.grammar_rule: Intransitive facial gesture verb requiring 'at' when directed toward a person.
examples: The baby smiled at her mother.
He smiled at me when I entered the room.
smile.common_mistake: ❌ She smiled to me friendly. ➔ ✅ She smiled at me in a friendly way.

stare at.definition: To look directly and fixedly at someone or something.
stare at.grammar_rule: Intransitive visual verb requiring 'at' when specifying the focus of the gaze.
examples: Don't stare at people; it is rude.
He stood staring at the night sky.
stare at.common_mistake: ❌ He stared to the screen. ➔ ✅ He stared at the screen.

glance at.definition: To take a brief or hurried look at something.
glance at.grammar_rule: Intransitive quick-look verb requiring 'at' before the object viewed.
glance at.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She glanced at her watch' ➔ Noun: 'A quick glance AT her watch'
examples: She glanced at her watch and realized she was late.
He glanced at the newspaper headlines before leaving.
glance at.common_mistake: ❌ She glanced to her phone. ➔ ✅ She glanced at her phone.

listen to.definition: To give attention to a sound or person speaking.
listen to.grammar_rule: Intransitive listening verb requiring 'to' whenever followed by an auditory target.
examples: I love to listen to podcasts while driving.
Please listen to your teacher carefully.
listen to.common_mistake: ❌ I listen music every day. ➔ ✅ I listen to music every day.

shout.definition: To utter a loud call or cry toward a person.
shout.grammar_rule: Use 'shout AT' to show anger. Use 'shout TO' so someone far away can hear you.
examples: Don't shout at me; I made an honest mistake.
He shouted to his friend across the noisy street.
shout.common_mistake: ❌ He shouted on me angrily. ➔ ✅ He shouted at me angrily.

live.pattern: live in [city / country] / live at [address] / live with [people]
live.definition: To reside or make one's home in a place or with someone.
live.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'in' for cities/countries, 'at' for specific addresses, and 'with' for housemates.
examples: I live in London with my family.
She lives at 42 Park Street.
live.common_mistake: ❌ I live to Rome. ➔ ✅ I live in Rome.

search.definition: To try to find someone or something by looking carefully.
search.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'for' when looking for a lost or sought item/person.
search.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Search for keys' ➔ Noun: 'In search OF keys'
examples: I am searching for my lost wallet.
They searched for answers in the old books.
search.common_mistake: ❌ I am searching my keys. ➔ ✅ I am searching for my keys.

phone.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb without preposition! Do NOT add 'to' when calling a person directly.
examples: I will phone you when I arrive at the station.
Did you phone your parents yesterday?
phone.common_mistake: ❌ I will phone to you tonight. ➔ ✅ I will phone you tonight.

email.definition: To send an electronic mail message to someone.
email.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT use 'to' after the verb 'email' before the recipient.
email.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'I emailed him' (no prep) ➔ Noun: 'I sent an email TO him'
examples: Please email the office if you have any questions.
I emailed the details to the whole team this morning.
email.common_mistake: ❌ Please email to me the file. ➔ ✅ Please email me the file.

greet.definition: To welcome or give a sign of recognition to someone.
greet.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! No preposition needed before the direct object.
greet.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'He greeted us' ➔ Noun: 'He gave a greeting TO us'
examples: The host warmly greeted all the guests at the door.
She greeted her old friend with a big hug.
greet.common_mistake: ❌ She greeted to everyone in the room. ➔ ✅ She greeted everyone in the room.

obey.definition: To carry out a command or follow a rule or law.
obey.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'with' after 'obey'.
examples: Drivers must obey traffic regulations at all times.
Children should obey their parents.
obey.common_mistake: ❌ You must obey to the rules. ➔ ✅ You must obey the rules.

survive.definition: To remain alive after a dangerous event or hardship.
survive.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb when referring to surviving an event! Do NOT use 'from' or 'to'.
survive.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'They survived the crash' ➔ Noun: 'Survival OF the crash'
examples: Few plants can survive extreme heat without water.
All passengers survived the emergency landing safely.
survive.common_mistake: ❌ He survived from the plane crash. ➔ ✅ He survived the plane crash.

enter.definition: To come or go into a place.
enter.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb when entering physical spaces! Do NOT use 'into'.
examples: Please enter the building through the main front door.
The doctor entered the room quietly.
enter.common_mistake: ❌ She entered into the classroom. ➔ ✅ She entered the classroom.

reach.definition: To arrive at or attain a place, goal, or stage.
reach.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'at' after 'reach'.
examples: We reached the hotel late in the evening.
The negotiators reached a final agreement after midnight.
reach.common_mistake: ❌ We reached to London at 5 PM. ➔ ✅ We reached London at 5 PM.

marry.definition: To join in marriage with someone.
marry.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb in active voice! Do NOT add 'with' or 'to' after active 'marry'.
marry.noun_parallel: ⚡ Active Verb: 'He married her' (no prep) ➔ Passive Adjective: 'He is married TO her'
examples: Will you marry me?
She married her high school sweetheart last year.
marry.common_mistake: ❌ He married with a lawyer. ➔ ✅ He married a lawyer.

resemble.definition: To look like or be similar to another person or thing.
resemble.grammar_rule: Direct transitive verb! Do NOT add 'to' or 'with' after 'resemble'.
resemble.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'She resembles her mother' ➔ Noun: 'She bears a resemblance TO her mother'
examples: The twins strongly resemble each other in appearance.
This new software resembles our old interface.
resemble.common_mistake: ❌ She resembles with her mother. ➔ ✅ She resembles her mother.

get on with.definition: To have a harmonious relationship with someone or continue work.
get on with.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'with' before a person or task.
examples: Do you get on with your new flatmates?
Let's get on with our work without wasting time.
get on with.common_mistake: ❌ I get on good my brother. ➔ ✅ I get on well with my brother.

check in.definition: To arrive and register at a hotel or airport.
check in.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. Use 'at' before the hotel or airport location.
check in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Check in at reception' ➔ Noun: 'Go to check-in'
examples: Guests can check in at the reception desk from 3 PM.
We checked in two hours before our flight.
check in.common_mistake: ❌ Check in into the hotel. ➔ ✅ Check in at the hotel.

check out.definition: To settle one's bill and leave a hotel.
check out.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. Use 'of' before the hotel being vacated.
examples: We need to check out of our room before eleven AM.
He checked out of the resort yesterday morning.
check out.common_mistake: ❌ We checked out from the room at 10. ➔ ✅ We checked out of the room at 10.

wake up.definition: To stop sleeping and become conscious.
wake up.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. Use 'at' when specifying exact time of waking.
examples: I usually wake up at seven o'clock on weekdays.
She woke up early to catch the morning train.
wake up.common_mistake: ❌ I wake up in 7 o'clock. ➔ ✅ I wake up at 7 o'clock.

work.pattern: work for [company] / work at [location] / work in [field]
work.definition: To be engaged in physical or mental activity as a job.
work.grammar_rule: Use 'work for' before an employer, 'work at' before a building, and 'work in' before an industry.
examples: She works for a multinational IT company.
He works in education as a teacher.
work.common_mistake: ❌ I work to Google. ➔ ✅ I work for Google.

stay.pattern: stay at [hotel] / stay in [city] / stay with [friends]
stay.definition: To remain in a particular place or lodge as a guest.
stay.grammar_rule: Use 'stay at' for hotels, 'stay in' for cities/countries, and 'stay with' for hosts.
examples: We stayed at a cozy hotel near the beach.
She is staying with her relatives in Rome.
stay.common_mistake: ❌ We stayed to a hotel. ➔ ✅ We stayed at a hotel.

complain.definition: To express dissatisfaction, pain, or annoyance about something.
complain.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'about' for the problem, 'to' for the recipient, and 'of' for medical symptoms.
complain.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Complain about noise' ➔ Noun: 'Make a complaint ABOUT noise'
examples: Neighbors complained about the noise late at night.
He complained to the manager about the cold food.
complain.common_mistake: ❌ She complained for the service. ➔ ✅ She complained about the service.

care.definition: To feel concern, interest, or affection for someone or something.
care.grammar_rule: Intransitive verb taking 'about' for importance/feelings, and 'for' when taking care of someone.
examples: He cares deeply about environmental issues.
She spent years caring for her elderly parents.
care.common_mistake: ❌ I don't care of your opinion. ➔ ✅ I don't care about your opinion.

dream.definition: To experience thoughts during sleep or imagine a desired future.
dream.grammar_rule: Use 'dream about' for sleep experiences and 'dream of' for ambitions or imagined possibilities.
examples: Last night I dreamed about flying over the ocean.
She dreams of becoming a professional musician.
dream.common_mistake: ❌ I dream for a new car. ➔ ✅ I dream of a new car.

prepare.definition: To make or get ready for a future event or task.
prepare.grammar_rule: Use direct transitive object when making an item ready, or 'prepare for' before an upcoming event.
prepare.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Prepare for exams' ➔ Noun: 'In preparation FOR exams'
examples: Students are preparing for their final examinations.
Chef prepared dinner for twenty guests.
prepare.common_mistake: ❌ We must prepare to the interview. ➔ ✅ We must prepare for the interview.

borrow.definition: To take and use something belonging to someone else with intention to return it.
borrow.grammar_rule: Direct object required! Use 'from' before the lender (do not confuse with 'lend to').
examples: Can I borrow a pen from you?
She borrowed a book from the local library.
borrow.common_mistake: ❌ Can I borrow money to you? ➔ ✅ Can I borrow money from you?

lend.definition: To grant temporary use of something on condition that it will be returned.
lend.grammar_rule: Direct object required! Use 'to' before the borrower (do not confuse with 'borrow from').
examples: I lent my umbrella to my colleague.
The bank agreed to lend money to small businesses.
lend.common_mistake: ❌ He lent his car from me. ➔ ✅ He lent his car to me.

look away.definition: To turn one's eyes away from someone or something.
look away.grammar_rule: Intransitive visual phrasal verb requiring 'from' when indicating the object avoided.
examples: She looked away from the scary scene on screen.
He looked away in embarrassment.
look away.common_mistake: ❌ She looked away to the accident. ➔ ✅ She looked away from the accident.

come back.pattern: come back to [place] / come back from [origin]
come back.definition: To return to a place or topic.
come back.grammar_rule: Intransitive directional phrasal verb. Use 'to' for return destination and 'from' for point of origin.
examples: When will you come back to London?
They just came back from vacation.
come back.common_mistake: ❌ He came back in home late. ➔ ✅ He came back home late.

go out.pattern: go out with [someone] / go out for [activity]
go out.definition: To leave home for social entertainment or be in a romantic relationship.
go out.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb using 'with' for companion/partner and 'for' for activity.
examples: We are going out for dinner tonight.
She has been going out with Mark for six months.
go out.common_mistake: ❌ We go out to dinner with. ➔ ✅ We are going out for dinner together.

get up.definition: To rise from bed or from a seated position.
get up.grammar_rule: Intransitive phrasal verb. Use 'at' for time and 'from' for bed or chair.
examples: I get up at six-thirty every morning.
He got up from his chair to open the door.
get up.common_mistake: ❌ I get up on 7 AM. ➔ ✅ I get up at 7 AM.

turn on.pattern: turn on [device / light] OR turn [it] on
turn on.definition: To start the operation of an appliance or light switch.
turn on.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Pronoun objects MUST go between verb and particle ('turn it on').
examples: Please turn on the lights when it gets dark.
Could you turn the radio on?
turn on.common_mistake: ❌ Turn on it please. ➔ ✅ Turn it on please.

turn off.pattern: turn off [device / light] OR turn [it] off
turn off.definition: To stop the operation of an appliance or light switch.
turn off.grammar_rule: Separable phrasal verb. Pronoun objects MUST go between verb and particle ('turn it off').
examples: Don't forget to turn off the computer before leaving.
He turned the television off.
turn off.common_mistake: ❌ Turn off it before bedtime. ➔ ✅ Turn it off before bedtime.

write to.definition: To send a letter or written communication to someone.
write to.grammar_rule: Intransitive in British/Standard English requiring 'to' before the recipient.
write to.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Write to customer service' ➔ Noun: 'A letter TO customer service'
examples: She wrote to her grandmother every month.
You should write to the council about this road issue.
write to.common_mistake: ❌ Write me a letter tomorrow. ➔ ✅ Write to me tomorrow.

belong in.definition: To be properly classified or located in a specific place.
belong in.grammar_rule: Intransitive positional phrasal verb taking 'in' for containers/rooms and 'on' for surfaces.
examples: These dirty dishes belong in the dishwasher.
That painting belongs on the main wall.
belong in.common_mistake: ❌ This book belongs at the shelf. ➔ ✅ This book belongs on the shelf.

walk out on.definition: To abandon or desert someone suddenly.
walk out on.grammar_rule: Inseparable multi-particle phrasal verb requiring 'on' before the abandoned party.
examples: He walked out on his family without any explanation.
You cannot just walk out on your job mid-shift.
walk out on.common_mistake: ❌ He walked out from his team. ➔ ✅ He walked out on his team.

talk about.definition: To converse or discuss a specific topic.
talk about.grammar_rule: Requires 'about' before the subject of discussion.
examples: We talked about our weekend plans over coffee.
What are you talking about?
talk about.common_mistake: ❌ We talked the movie. ➔ ✅ We talked about the movie.

agree with.definition: To have the same opinion as someone else.
agree with.grammar_rule: Inseparable phrasal verb requiring 'with' when agreeing with a person.
examples: I agree with you completely on this point.
She rarely agrees with her manager.
agree with.common_mistake: ❌ I am agree with you. ➔ ✅ I agree with you.

agree to.definition: To give consent or accept a proposal or terms.
agree to.grammar_rule: Use 'agree to' before proposals, conditions, or terms.
examples: They agreed to the terms of the contract.
She agreed to help us with the project.
agree to.common_mistake: ❌ She agreed with the proposal. ➔ ✅ She agreed to the proposal.

apologize to.definition: To express regret to a person.
apologize to.grammar_rule: Requires 'to' before the person receiving the apology.
examples: You should apologize to her right away.
He apologized to his colleagues.
apologize to.common_mistake: ❌ Apologize her now. ➔ ✅ Apologize to her now.

arrive at.definition: To reach a specific building, station, or decision point.
arrive at.grammar_rule: Use 'arrive at' for specific locations, buildings, airports, or conclusions. NEVER 'to'!
examples: We arrived at the station five minutes late.
They arrived at a consensus after long debate.
arrive at.common_mistake: ❌ Arrive to the airport. ➔ ✅ Arrive at the airport.

arrive in.definition: To reach a city, town, or country.
arrive in.grammar_rule: Use 'arrive in' for large geographic areas, cities, and countries. NEVER 'to'!
examples: The plane arrived in Tokyo on time.
When did you arrive in London?
arrive in.common_mistake: ❌ We arrived to France yesterday. ➔ ✅ We arrived in France yesterday.

believe in.definition: To feel confident in the truth, existence, or value of something.
believe in.grammar_rule: Requires 'in' when expressing faith in existence or confidence in abilities.
believe in.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Believe in success' ➔ Noun: 'Have belief IN success'
examples: Do you believe in ghosts?
I believe in your ability to succeed.
believe in.common_mistake: ❌ I believe on you. ➔ ✅ I believe in you.

pay for.definition: To give money in exchange for goods, services, or face consequences.
pay for.grammar_rule: Use 'pay for' before the item or service being purchased.
examples: I will pay for the dinner tonight.
He had to pay for his past mistakes.
pay for.common_mistake: ❌ I paid the coffee. ➔ ✅ I paid for the coffee.

speak with.definition: To engage in a conversation with someone.
speak with.grammar_rule: Requires 'with' or 'to' before the person spoken to.
examples: I spoke with the manager regarding my account.
Can I speak with you for a moment?
speak with.common_mistake: ❌ Speak at me. ➔ ✅ Speak with me.

talk to.definition: To address or speak to a person.
examples: She went to talk to the doctor.
Don't talk to strangers on the internet.
talk to.common_mistake: ❌ Talk at him politely. ➔ ✅ Talk to him politely.

confer on.definition: To grant or bestow a title, degree, or honor upon someone.
confer on.grammar_rule: Transitive formal verb requiring direct object (honor/title) followed by 'on' or 'upon' + recipient.
confer on.noun_parallel: ⚡ Verb: 'Confer an honor on him' ➔ Noun: 'Conferral OF an honor'
examples: The university will confer an honorary degree on the visiting scholar.
The president conferred a medal on the hero.
confer on.common_mistake: ❌ Confer a title to him. ➔ ✅ Confer a title on him.

desist from.definition: To cease or stop doing something.
desist from.grammar_rule: Formal inseparable phrasal verb requiring 'from' + gerund (-ing).
examples: The court ordered them to desist from illegal activities.
They desisted from further protests after the meeting.
desist from.common_mistake: ❌ Desist to take action. ➔ ✅ Desist from taking action.
